_about: Regression registry. Every notable bug we have shipped and fixed, with the test that now guards it. The guide's rule: a bug is not 'done' until a test makes it impossible to reintroduce silently. The actual gate is `pytest` in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml); this file is the human- and agent-readable index of bug -> guard so a cold-start agent learns the gotchas and never re-opens a closed bug. Add an entry whenever you fix a bug. Prune an entry only after its guard has held for 6+ months and the area was rewritten.

_schema.root_cause: the actual reason, not the symptom
_schema.guard: test file::test_name that now fails if this regresses
_schema.lesson: the generalizable rule to carry forward

bugs.symptom: Lone single 'standard'-tier hires (noise) kept appearing in Discovery even though the on-demand panel parked them. The daily cron re-admitted the noise the panel would have hidden.
bugs.root_cause: The park decision lived only on the on-demand panel-annotation path. The cron ingestion path never called it, so the two paths disagreed.
bugs.lesson: A gate must run on EVERY ingestion path (cron AND panel). When you add a filter, test cron/panel parity, not just the path you are looking at.

bugs.symptom: ~692 historical job signals mis-ranked intent: a 'standard'-tier role scored as 'core' on re-evaluation.
bugs.root_cause: The RCM tier was denormalized onto the signal but not persisted on older records; when missing, the points logic defaulted to 'core' (too high).
bugs.lesson: When a denormalized field may be absent on old rows, derive it from the durable field (here role -> rcm_titles.tier_for_role) and fail to the SAFE default, not the generous one.

bugs.symptom: Accounts freshly demoted to needs_review could be auto-rejected almost immediately.
bugs.root_cause: The auto-reject TTL measured the age of the underlying signal, not how long the account had been in the review state.
bugs.lesson: A state TTL must be measured from the state-entry timestamp (entered_review_at), never from the data's age. Promote-on-reheat applies only to decayed accounts.

bugs.symptom: Importing a CSV that already contained accounts present in Discovery created duplicate 'twin' rows.
bugs.root_cause: Two id schemes (acc_<key> for promoted, csv_<slug> for imports) were not reconciled at import time, so the same company existed under two ids.
bugs.lesson: Dedupe on identity ACROSS id schemes at the import boundary. Moving a Discovery record into Scored (carrying its signals) beats creating a new one.

bugs.symptom: The auto-score toggle silently flipped back to OFF after any browser reload.
bugs.root_cause: The toggle state lived only in React memory; nothing persisted it across reloads.
bugs.lesson: Any operator toggle that must survive a reload needs persistence (localStorage) AND a UI regression test that reloads and re-asserts.

bugs.symptom: A bad JSX edit or a reference to a non-existent Icons.* white-screened the WHOLE app at runtime, and pytest stayed green.
bugs.root_cause: There is no compile step. Babel transpiles in the browser, so a syntax error or undefined component is a runtime failure invisible to backend tests.
bugs.lesson: In-browser JSX has no compile gate, so the Playwright UI smoke IS the compile gate. Transpile-check JSX and run the UI smoke before every deploy. Only use Icons.* that exist in ui.jsx.

bugs.symptom: A single stray like on a competitor's post created a low-value 'signal', cluttering Discovery.
bugs.root_cause: Social engagement qualified on any single interaction, with no per-person threshold and no competitor-vs-own distinction.
bugs.lesson: Engagement qualifies only on intent-bearing volume (a comment, or 2+ likes) and ONLY for competitor accounts, not our own (getMagical). Collect multiple touches per person, then decide.

bugs.symptom: Engagement sync 500'd. POST /v3/reporting/emails with a from/to that carried a timezone offset ('2026-05-15T00:00:00+00:00') returned 500 Internal Server Error; date-only ('2026-05-15') and Z-suffixed datetimes returned 200.
bugs.root_cause: datetime.isoformat() emits a '+00:00' offset, which Reply.io's report endpoint cannot parse. The reporting window is day-granular, so a bare date is the right shape.
bugs.lesson: Send the reporting from/to as a bare 'YYYY-MM-DD' date. Verify connectors against the LIVE API, not just mocks — a mock happily accepts the bad format; only the real endpoint reveals the 500.

bugs.symptom: After bumping the Health System rubric to 30 pts, the Scored board re-resolved the flat tier keys + denominator but the tier BADGE the UI renders (the nested `tier` object) stayed stale: the ring showed X/30 while the badge still said the old Tier 1.
bugs.root_cause: _retier rewrote tier_band/tier_label/max_total but not the nested tier:{band,label} object the UI actually reads via `a.tier || tierFor(...)`.
bugs.lesson: When you re-resolve a denormalized value, rewrite EVERY representation the readers use (flat keys AND the nested object). Grep the UI for the field it actually reads; a test that only checks the JSON flat key passes while the screen is wrong.

bugs.symptom: The Slack AE card + Activity view showed the stale stored fit tier after the rubric change, disagreeing with the Scored board.
bugs.root_cause: _classify trusted the stored tier_label; the re-tier fix was applied only to the scored-list endpoint, not the engagement read path (a half-fix).
bugs.lesson: A re-resolution must cover ALL read surfaces. Centralize it in one shared helper (_resolve_scored_band) and call it at every seam, not just the one you first noticed.

bugs.symptom: The Hot-account AE Slack lead line never fired; resolve_ae returned None for every account, so the whole AE-tag feature was dead on the real path.
bugs.root_cause: _classify emitted the human framework LABEL ('Health System') but resolve_ae / SPECIALTY_AE are keyed by the raw key ('health_system'); the specialty lookup always missed. Unit tests passed the raw key directly, masking it.
bugs.lesson: Never route/look-up on a display label. Carry the raw key (framework_key) for lookups and reserve the label for rendering; test the integration path, not just the pure function with ideal inputs.

bugs.symptom: Folding every source (Reply.io, SFDC, podcast, LinkedIn TOFU) into POST /api/engagement/sync meant the background job could fire real SFDC/Apify/Reply.io calls during tests, since the sync handler schedules the coro on the live lifespan loop — only run_sync was stubbed.
bugs.root_cause: The shared client fixture stubbed run_sync but not run_sfdc_sync / run_podcast_url_sync / linkedin_ads_runner.run, and the new orchestrator calls all of them in the background.
bugs.lesson: When a background job grows new legs, stub EVERY leg in the fixture (no leg makes real network I/O in tests) and assert best-effort: a leg raising must not skip the rest.

bugs.area: engagement heat view + repos + UI/Slack labels (sales_accepted_opportunity)
bugs.symptom: SAO was 'dropped' in the 2026-06 review (sync stopped pulling it), but 18 of the top 40 accounts still showed 'Sales accepted opp' (+10) in heat, drawer, momentum, and Slack — because historical SAO events stayed in storage with points baked in, and the heat SQL view + label maps still counted them.
bugs.root_cause: Dropping a signal at the INGEST layer (sync) doesn't remove already-stored events. Heat is summed in the engaged_accounts SQL view from stored points, so retired-but-stored kinds keep counting until excluded at the READ layer.
bugs.lesson: Retiring a signal needs a READ-layer exclusion (DEPRECATED_KINDS), not just stopping ingest. Apply it everywhere heat/events are read — the SQL view (re-applied via ensure_schema on deploy), both repos' events/series/recent, plus the UI/Slack label maps — so stored history stays for audit but never counts or shows.

bugs.symptom: Before a multi-AE/SDR rollout: the 'already activated' dedup lived only in the browser (localStorage), so two reps (or the auto-route loop across browsers/reloads) could activate the SAME Hot account → it posted to Slack twice and double-spent enrichment. Same root cause as the FullEnrich credit incident.
bugs.root_cause: Per-browser dedup is per-user, not global, and the in-process run-locks don't cover per-account activation. No server-side record of what was already activated.
bugs.lesson: Dedup that guards spend/external posts must be SERVER-SIDE and race-safe: claim the resource atomically (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) BEFORE any paid/visible work, short-circuit the loser, and release the claim if the work fails so it can retry. Client-side dedup is a convenience, never the authority.

bugs.symptom: Live LinkedIn TOFU runs reported airtable_failed and leads never landed in Airtable — every write 422'd. Not auth (key worked) and not bad columns (all field names matched). The table already had 2 rows per Email (a Clay workflow also writes it).
bugs.root_cause: upsert used Airtable's native performUpsert with fieldsToMergeOn=[Email], which returns HTTP 422 when MORE THAN ONE existing row matches the merge key. A second writer (Clay) had created duplicate Email rows, so the merge could not resolve to one record.
bugs.lesson: Don't rely on a vendor's merge-on-key upsert when another system also writes the table — it assumes ≤1 match. Do an explicit find-then-update-first-or-create (dup-tolerant), which never 422s and never adds another duplicate. When a 4xx says 'unprocessable', capture the response BODY — 422 means data/semantics rejected, distinct from 401/403 auth.

bugs.symptom: An account could get stuck permanently 'already_activated' with no Slack post: claim_activation() inserted the ledger row, but if _engaged_one()/enrichment/resolve threw BEFORE the Slack post, the claim was never released (release only ran on the Slack-failed path). Every future click then returned already_activated with no spend and no post; only force=true could recover it.
bugs.root_cause: The atomic claim was taken before a block of work that wasn't all under a try/except that releases on failure — only the explicit Slack-post-failed branch released. Any earlier exception leaked the claim.
bugs.lesson: When you CLAIM a resource before doing work, the ENTIRE work block (not just the last step) must run under a guard that releases the claim on ANY failure. A claim-before-work pattern needs claim → try/except-release → succeed.

bugs.symptom: A merge value containing an apostrophe (e.g. o'brien@x.com) built a malformed Airtable formula — the dup-tolerant upsert's lookup would miss the existing row and CREATE a duplicate, defeating the dedup it exists to provide.
bugs.root_cause: The formula wrapped the value in single quotes and SQL-style-escaped embedded quotes (\'), which Airtable's formula grammar does not honor.
bugs.lesson: Each query language has its own string-literal escaping — don't assume SQL rules. Airtable formulas: wrap the literal in DOUBLE quotes and escape only \ and "; an apostrophe is then literal. Match the target grammar, not a familiar one.

bugs.symptom: CI lint-and-test went red on every push: test_sync_runs_all_sources_best_effort failed with 'AIRTABLE_BASE_ID / AIRTABLE_LINKEDIN_TABLE not set' — the LinkedIn sync leg crashed constructing AirtableClient before reaching the mocked runner, so 'linkedin' was never recorded. It PASSED locally and only failed in CI.
bugs.root_cause: The fixture stubbed linkedin_ads_runner.run but NOT the AirtableClient/ReplyioClient that _linkedin_tofu constructs BEFORE calling the runner. Those constructors need AIRTABLE_*/REPLYIO env, which exists locally via .env (load_dotenv) but not in CI — a hidden env dependency that 'works on my machine' masked.
bugs.lesson: Tests must be env-independent: stub EVERY external client a code path constructs, not just the one that does I/O. 'Passes locally' is worthless when local .env supplies vars CI lacks — reproduce CI by moving .env aside. And verify the way CI does (ruff check . over the whole repo + bare pytest), not a narrower scoped command.

bugs.symptom: A new GET /api/engagement/live-routing returned {'detail':'account not found'} — it was matched by the earlier GET /api/engagement/{id} account route (id='live-routing'), not the new handler.
bugs.root_cause: FastAPI matches routes in registration order; a single-segment path under /api/engagement/ collides with the /api/engagement/{id} catch-all unless registered BEFORE it (like inbox/sync are). The new route was defined after {id}.
bugs.lesson: Don't add a single-segment route after a sibling /{id} catch-all. Either register it earlier, or use a 2-segment namespaced path (e.g. /api/engagement/settings/live-routing, like /api/engagement/activations/reset) so {id} can't swallow it.

bugs.symptom: A Salesforce meeting SCHEDULED in the future (StartDateTime 2026-07-09 while today was 2026-06-25) was stored with that future occurred_at. It showed a future timeline entry ('Meeting booked Jul 9'), inflated current heat, and trivially passed the June-25 send cutoff (future >= cutoff) — so under permanent-live it would have pushed the account to AEs/SDRs off a meeting that had not happened.
bugs.root_cause: parse() used StartDateTime (the meeting time, which can be in the future for a scheduled meeting) as the engagement signal date. The signal (a meeting was booked) actually occurs at CreatedDate.
bugs.lesson: An engagement signal's date is when the SIGNAL happened, not a scheduled future time. Use CreatedDate (booking) when StartDateTime is in the future, AND clamp occurred_at to now at the storage layer so no source can ever persist a future date. Future dates silently corrupt every date-gated rule downstream (send cutoff, momentum windows, recency).

bugs.symptom: Found in pre-go-live QA: activating a Lower-tier account computed notify=False (no AE/SDR owner, dm_limit=0) but STILL called activate_account, so a direct API activation of a Lower account would drop an ownerless card into a real channel when live. The UI hides Activate for Lower and auto-route skips it, so it was only reachable by a direct/scripted call.
bugs.root_cause: The notify flag gated enrichment + owner but not the post itself; the spec is 'Lower -> no handoff', i.e. no post at all.
bugs.lesson: When a tier/branch means 'do nothing', short-circuit the SIDE EFFECT (the post), not just its inputs. Don't rely on the UI to keep an unsafe endpoint path unreachable; guard it server-side. Release any dedup claim taken before the early return so the account isn't left stuck 'activated'.

bugs.symptom: The AE lookup card never showed the 'Engaging' chip even for accounts with real heat (e.g. the seeded Warm/16 account).
bugs.root_cause: The helper matched name/domain/tier keys against the RAW engaged_accounts SQL view, which carries only account_id + counters. Those fields exist only on the SHAPED board rows (_engaged_view()), so nothing ever matched.
bugs.fix: The endpoint passes _engaged_view() rows (names/tiers resolved) into the pure helper; the helper documents that contract.

bugs.symptom: A fit score could claim 'no public intent signals found' about an account that BOOKED A MEETING with us. Live: Synergy Orthopedic (engagement Hot, heat 22, meeting booked 2026-06-25) scored intent 4/10 'no signals'; Humana (heat 84, 3 booked meetings) scored intent 3/10. Audit found 3 such blindspots + 4 engaged accounts with unverified QA.
bugs.root_cause: The scorer's inputs were public web research + carried DISCOVERY signals only; the ENGAGEMENT store (meetings, BOFU forms, ad engagement) was never fed in. The AE-lookup card showed the heat chip, but the score never saw the events — card and score contradicted each other.
bugs.fix: engagement/intent_feed.to_intent_signals (events -> scorer signal dicts) + ScoringService(own_signals=...) merges them at SCORE time on every path (ae/promote/rescore/batch; no silent board-wide shifts — scores change only when a score runs). app.py provider matches by normalized-name key then domain via the shaped board (names drift, domains don't — the Riverview csv/AKA case). ae-lookup commits persist the signals for drawer provenance.
bugs.guard: tests/test_intent_feed.py (mapping/collapse/orders + service merge dedupes + provider failure never blocks) ; live before/after: Synergy 16->22 (intent 4->9), Humana intent 3->8 citing '3 meetings booked'.

bugs.area: campaigns / catalog (ICP -> sequence routing + Reply.io auto-detect)
bugs.symptom: "Engagement Anesthesiology" got no suggested sequence in the Campaigns tab; American-spelled anesthesia accounts would route to specialty_other instead of the anesthesia sequence.
bugs.root_cause: The vertical regex was an[ae]esthes — a character CLASS demands one letter between "an" and "esthes", which matches British "anaesthes" but never American "anesthes". Wanted an optional letter (ana?esthes), wrote a mandatory one.
bugs.lesson: A char class [xy] is one-of, not maybe-one: optional letters are x? / a?. Verify keyword routing against REAL source data (the live Reply.io names caught this), not only invented fixtures.
